generatedProse.concept-context: In your subject, the honest process is the same. You start from your own view of the task, use AI within the category your brief sets, and treat everything it gives you as a draft to check, not an answer to submit. You log what you did as you go, so the declaration almost writes itself. The evidence trail - your dated drafts, notes and saved chats - is what shows, if anyone asks, that the work and the thinking are yours.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two sport science students, writing a report whose brief allows AI as Category 2.

{{learner-a}} skips the planning, asks a chatbot to write a section, and pastes it in with light edits. {{learner-a}} keeps a reference the tool supplied without checking it, writes no record of the use, and adds no declaration. The work is the tool’s, a source may be invented, and nothing shows {{learner-a}}’s own understanding.

{{learner-b}} thinks first and notes a line of argument, then uses the tool to suggest an angle, not a finished answer. {{learner-b}} fact-checks every claim against real sources, keeps the chat and the drafts, and writes a short declaration naming the tool, how it was used, and the prompts and outputs.

Both had the same permission. Only {{learner-b}} used AI honestly and could show the work was their own.
generatedProse.summary: When a brief allows AI, Cardiff Met's six-step process keeps your use honest. You think first, design your prompt, develop the dialogue, critically evaluate the output, log your use, and check for red flags before you submit. Two habits sit alongside it. You declare your use - Acknowledge the tool and publisher, Describe how you used it, and Evidence the prompts and outputs. You also keep an evidence trail: dated drafts, notes and saved chats. Together with the rule, the categories and misconduct, you can now use AI honestly where it is allowed, and show that the work is your own.

check.body: You have used AI within the category your brief allows on an assignment in {{context}}. What is the best way to be ready if anyone questions the work?

items.text: Keep an evidence trail - dated drafts, notes, and AI chats saved at the time - and declare your use.
Delete the AI chats so there is nothing to find.
Say nothing about AI and hope it is not noticed.
Rewrite everything at the last minute to look different.

feedback.correct: That's right. An evidence trail plus a clear declaration is your strongest protection.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Hiding or deleting your use is risky; a kept evidence trail and a declaration protect you.
